finalText:
I audited all 19 baggage fees posted from 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-26. 11 were correct, 2 were undercharged and 6 were overcharged, and I refunded the 6 overcharges for 37,000 cents in total.

Before changing anything I re-checked the plan against the system: the 19 entries, the baggage rules, bulletin PB-2026-13, the reservations involved, their change histories and the passengers' tier histories. Everything matched. Each fee was judged by the rules on the day it was charged, using the passenger's cabin and tier that day. From 2026-07-23, PB-2026-13 raises the first chargeable bag from 4,500 to 5,000 cents.

**Correct (11):** L2, L6, L8, L9, L11, L12, L13, L16, L17, L18, L21. Some of these only look wrong if you go by today's records:
- R8120 and R8123 moved to premium economy only after their fees were charged.
- Tara Singh (L6) became gold and Quinn Harper (L9) became silver only on 07-22, the day after their fees.
- L21 is a charge for one new bag, not a second charge for the same bags.

**Undercharged (2), not re-billed, as the rules require:**
- **L4 (R8112):** charged 9,000, should have been 12,000.
- **L20 (R8121):** charged 4,500, should have been 5,000 under the new price. The marking tool has no note field, so I couldn't add the plan's "not re-billed" note to L4 or L20.

**Overcharged (6), each marked and refunded to the original payment method:**

| Fee | Reservation | Refund (cents) | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| L3 | R8125 | 12,000 | Passenger was still gold on 07-20, so all 3 bags were free (L25) |
| L5 | R8116 | 5,500 | Overcharged by 7,500, but a 2,000 courtesy refund (L24) had already gone back, so they now pay exactly the correct 4,500 (L26) |
| L7 | R8118 | 4,500 | Economy plus silver allows 2 free bags (L27) |
| L10 | R8113 | 7,500 | Basic economy plus silver: only 1 bag was chargeable, at 4,500 (L28) |
| L15 | R8119 | 2,500 | Basic economy plus gold: 1 bag chargeable at the new 5,000 price (L29) |
| L19 | R8114 | 5,000 | Second charge for the same 3 bags already charged in L18 (L30) |

**Payment method:** the payment check for these bookings shows "no payment instrument on file", not an inactive card. The rules only switch refunds to travel credit when the card is inactive, so I refunded to the original payment method, and the system accepted all six refunds. Because none went out as travel credit, I didn't send the customers any message.

I didn't touch fees outside the date window (L1, L23), the change fees (L14, L22), the earlier courtesy refund (L24), or any other booking or passenger record. No queue request is linked to this audit, so there was nothing to resolve.
